plan.as_committed_day_one:
# Sprint 2 Plan

**Goal:** Turn ShiftSwap into something the circulation desk crew at the campus library could use for real: a rebuilt UI with clear flows and empty, loading and error states, a reader that turns a photo of the paper schedule into shifts, and a manager approval step for every swap. Then spend the rest of the sprint on discovery with student employees, ending with 3-5 ranked ideas for what to build next.

**Why this:** In Sprint 1 the app worked only if shifts were typed in by hand, and nobody on the crew will do that. The photo reader removes that step. The approval step is what the desk manager said she needs before she would let anyone use it. The discovery is because I have only talked to myself about this problem so far, and I want the next sprint to come from what other student employees say.

**Done looks like:**
- **ShiftSwap:** a student can post a shift, a coworker can pick it up, and the manager can approve or decline it, all on the live app. The UI is rebuilt on shadcn/ui with empty, loading and error states. A photo of the paper schedule becomes a draft of shifts that the student can edit and undo before saving. Students see only their own shifts and swaps. The manager and both students get a text message when a swap changes.
- **Discovery:** interviews with at least 5 student employees, a short brief for each of 3-5 ideas (the problem, who has it, and the evidence it matters), and a ranking that picks one for Sprint 3.

**Predicted difficulty:** 4

**Done looks like:**
- **ShiftSwap:** a student can post a shift, a coworker can pick it up, and the manager can approve or decline it, all on the live app. The UI is rebuilt on shadcn/ui with empty, loading and error states. A photo of the paper schedule becomes a draft of shifts that the student can edit and undo before saving. Students see only their own shifts and swaps. The manager and both students get an email when a swap changes. Text message alerts are not required this sprint.
- **Discovery:** interviews with at least 5 student employees, a short brief for each of 3-5 ideas (the problem, who has it, and the evidence it matters), and a ranking that picks one for Sprint 3.

**Predicted difficulty:** 4

**Change (Oct 6):** Text message alerts are no longer required. Email through Resend covers the same need for now. Text messages cost money per message and need a verified phone number for every student, and I want the crew to try the app before I pay for anything.

**Actual difficulty:** 5

**Why it differed:** Row-level security took much longer than I expected. I did not understand how a policy decides which rows a person can see, and I had to work through it table by table before the manager view and the student view both worked.

**Retro:** I hit my goal. Posting, picking up and approving a shift all work on the live app, and the photo reader turned this week's paper schedule into 64 shifts that I only had to fix in two places. The UI is rebuilt with real empty and error states, which I had skipped in Sprint 1. I interviewed 6 student employees and the desk manager, wrote five idea briefs, and ranked them. I picked open-shift alerts for Sprint 3. I also started using a subagent to turn my interview notes into themes while I kept building.

What changes next sprint:
- I want to understand row-level security well enough to write a policy without trial and error.
- I'll test each feature on my phone before I commit it, because most of the crew will use ShiftSwap on a phone.
- I'll ask two people from the crew to use the app for a real swap and write down where they get stuck.
- I'll keep a short log of each decision I make about the data, so I can explain it to the manager.

# Sprint 2 Review

**Window:** 2026-09-28 (plan committed 8:14 PM) to 2026-10-12
**Sessions reviewed:** 11 in 1 project (0 sessions excluded). Some of them started before the window; only activity after the plan commit is counted.

## When you worked

You were active on 11 of the 15 days (Sep 28, 29; Oct 1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 11, 12). That's 142 prompts and 38 commits. The work was spread out, with three peaks:
- **Oct 1 to 2:** the UI rebuild on shadcn/ui: shift board, post and pick-up flows, empty and error states, design tokens.
- **Oct 6:** the busiest day of the sprint (47 prompts, 14 commits).
- **Oct 10 to 12:** the double-booking fix and discovery, then a run of manager and week-view features (58 prompts across the three days).

Sep 30, Oct 3, Oct 4 and Oct 9 had no activity. Oct 5 had one prompt.

## Where you got stuck

- **Row-level security for swaps (Oct 6).** About 20 prompts went back and forth over the policies:
  - The first policy let a student read every swap at the location, so the manager view and the student view looked the same.
  - The manager role was checked from the sign-in token, which did not carry it, so approvals failed with a permission error.
  - SQL had to be pasted into the Supabase editor again after a policy name collided with an old one.
  - It ended the same day: students read only swaps they posted or picked up, and only the decide route can change a swap's status.
- **Double-booked shifts after a re-scan (Oct 8 to 10).**
  - On Oct 8, a re-scan of the updated paper schedule inserted every shift a second time. Nine shifts showed twice, and three students looked double-booked on the week view.
  - On Oct 10, the first cleanup query deleted both copies of two shifts and had to be undone from the import history.
  - It ended Oct 10 with a unique key on each shift (person, start, end, location), re-scans that update matching shifts instead of adding them, and the nine duplicates removed.
- **The conflict check on pick-up (Oct 11 to 12).** The request was rephrased three times.
  - First the check ran only at the confirm step, so a student found out about a conflict after choosing the shift.
  - Then the check ignored class times saved in the profile.
  - Then overlapping shifts were hidden from the week view instead of marked.
  - Each was fixed in turn, ending with overlapping shifts marked and the Pick up button disabled with the reason (`71c0e5b`).

## What took the most time

By prompt volume, **Oct 6 was a third of the sprint** (47 of 142 prompts):
- The schedule photo reader, with its draft table and structured output
- The check-schedule-import skill
- The manager approval flow and email notices
- Row-level security for swaps
- Logging progress

**Oct 10 was next** (25 prompts). It was split between the double-booking fix and discovery: writing the interview-synthesizer agent and running it on notes from seven interviews.

**Oct 11 to 12** (33 prompts) went into the board and the manager queue:
- Keyboard support and undo in the draft table
- Shift notes
- The conflict check
- Decline reasons
- Empty states for managers, import history and an error state for the photo reader

Discovery took roughly 15 prompts in all.

## Axis

**Application Architecture**, with Design a close second. The biggest single block of time went into data and access work: the photo reader's server route, swap tables, row-level security, the manager role, and the re-scan fix. UI work came close behind (the shadcn/ui rebuild, the week view, states off the happy path, the approval queue).

## Against your plan

**Goal was:** a rebuilt UI with clear flows and states, a schedule-photo reader, and a manager approval step, usable by the circulation desk crew; then discovery with student employees ending with 3-5 ranked ideas.

**Met.**

| Done looks like | Result |
|---|---|
| Post, pick up and approve work end to end on the live app | Met. All three flows run on shiftswap.example.com (`b2c08e1`, `b5d0e72`) |
| UI rebuilt on shadcn/ui with empty, loading and error states | Met. Rebuilt Oct 2 (`3f1a9c2`), loading states Oct 8, more empty and error states Oct 12 |
| Schedule photo becomes an editable draft with undo | Met (`c94d1b0`, `16f9a3c`). The Oct 8 re-scan double-booked nine shifts; fixed Oct 10 |
| Students see only their own shifts and swaps | Met. Row-level security on shifts (Sprint 1) and swaps (`6e4f13a`) |
| Manager and students notified when a swap changes | Met by email (`b2c08e1`). Text messages were dropped by the Oct 6 plan change |
| Interviews with at least 5 student employees | Met. Notes from 6 student employees and the desk manager in `sprints/discovery/interviews/` |
| A brief for each of 3-5 ideas | Met. Five briefs in `sprints/discovery/` |
| A ranking that picks one for Sprint 3 | Met. `ranking.md` scores all five; on Oct 12 it picked open-shift alerts, which was not the top-scored idea, and gives the reason |

## Retro

Answers are also in `sprint-2-plan.md`.

**Actual difficulty:** 5 (predicted 4)

**Why it differed:** Row-level security took much longer than I expected. I did not understand how a policy decides which rows a person can see, and I had to work through it table by table before the manager view and the student view both worked.

**Did you hit the goal?** Yes. Posting, picking up and approving a shift all work on the live app, and the photo reader turned this week's paper schedule into 64 shifts that I only had to fix in two places. I interviewed 6 student employees and the desk manager, wrote five idea briefs, and picked open-shift alerts for Sprint 3.

**What happened:** The UI is rebuilt with real empty and error states, which I had skipped in Sprint 1. I also started using a subagent to turn my interview notes into themes while I kept building.

- I'll ask two people from the crew to use the app for a real swap and write down where they get stuck.
- I'll keep a short log of each decision I make about the data, so I can explain it to the manager.

# Sprint 3 Plan

**Goal:** Put ShiftSwap in front of the circulation desk crew for real swaps, and add open-shift alerts: when a shift is posted, every student who is free at that time and under 20 hours that week gets an email, and the first one to accept it sends it to the manager. Keep the two Sprint 2 retro commitments: test on a phone before each commit, and log each data decision.

**Why this:** The ranking scored automatic scheduling from availability higher, but the manager said in her interview that the real pain is shifts that nobody picks up, and alerts can be built and tried in two weeks. The crew starts a new schedule on Oct 26, which is a natural time to switch from the group chat.

**Done looks like:**
- When a shift is posted, only students who are free and under 20 hours that week get an alert.
- The first student to accept gets the shift sent to the manager; everyone else sees it is taken.
- At least 4 crew members complete a real swap through ShiftSwap.
- The manager approves at least one swap from her phone without help.
- Sprint 2 retro: every commit tested on a phone first, and a decision log in `docs/decisions.md`.

**Predicted difficulty:** 3
readme:
# ShiftSwap

## Context

**What I'm building:** ShiftSwap, an app for student employees at a campus job. A student who
cannot work a shift posts it, a coworker picks it up, and the manager approves the swap. One AI
feature reads the shifts from a photo of the paper schedule, so nobody has to type them in.

**My role:** Solo builder, using Claude Code as my development partner.

**My user:** Student employees at the campus library circulation desk (14 people), and their
manager, who approves every swap.

## Where the work lives

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| ShiftSwap code (app, photo reader, swap flow, tests) | This repo: `app/`, `components/`, `lib/`, `supabase/migrations/`, `tests/` |
| Live app | https://shiftswap.example.com (sign in with a test account; each student sees only their own shifts) |
| Database | Supabase. Schema and row-level security policies are in `supabase/migrations/` |
| Sprint plans, reviews and progress logs | `sprints/` |
| Sprint 2 discovery: interview notes, 5 idea briefs, ranking | `sprints/discovery/` |
| Custom skill and agent | `.claude/skills/check-schedule-import/`, `.claude/agents/interview-synthesizer.md` |

## How ShiftSwap works

| Step | Who | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| Import | Manager or student | Upload a photo of the paper schedule; the reader returns a draft of shifts to check, edit and save |
| Post | Student | Pick one of your shifts, add a note, and post it to the board |
| Pick up | Coworker | Open a posted shift, see any conflict with your own shifts, and pick it up |
| Approve | Manager | Approve or decline in the queue; approving moves the shift to the new person |
| Notice | Everyone involved | An email goes to both students and the manager when a swap changes |

### Run it locally

```
pnpm install
pnpm dev
```

The app opens at http://localhost:3000. It needs a `.env.local` with `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`,
`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `RESEND_API_KEY`. The file is gitignored.

### The schedule photo reader

The route in `app/api/schedule-photo/route.ts` sends the photo to a vision model and asks for
structured output: each shift's person, day, start, end and location, with a confidence flag.
The result comes back as a draft. Nothing is saved until the student reviews it: any row can be
edited or removed, Undo restores the last change, and low-confidence rows are highlighted. The
photo is deleted after the draft is saved, because the paper schedule lists phone numbers.

### Tests

```
pnpm test
```

Tests cover the time parser, the draft table's undo, and the swap rules (who can read a swap,
and who can approve one).

---
name: check-schedule-import
description: Check a ShiftSwap schedule draft against the photo it came from before it is saved. Reads the draft the import page wrote (imports/_work/draft.json) and the photo, lists every shift that looks wrong and why, and writes draft-checked.json, which the import page opens for review. Use when the user says "/check-schedule-import", "check the draft", or "check this schedule".
---

# Check a schedule draft

The import page (`pnpm dev`, http://localhost:3000/import) has a **Check in Claude Code** button. It writes the draft and the photo to `imports/_work/`. This skill reads both and writes a checked draft back.

## Steps

1. Read `imports/_work/draft.json`. Each row has `person`, `day`, `start`, `end`, `location` and `confidence`.
2. Open `imports/_work/photo.jpg` and find the same grid: days across the top, names down the side.
3. For each row, check the cell it came from. Flag a row when:
   - the time in the cell does not match `start` or `end`
   - the name is not on the roster in `imports/_work/roster.json`
   - two rows give the same person overlapping times on the same day
   - a cell in the photo has a time but no row in the draft
4. Do not change a row you are unsure about. Mark it `needs_review` with a one-line reason.
5. Write `imports/_work/draft-checked.json` with the same rows, each with `status` (`ok`, `fixed` or `needs_review`) and `reason`.
6. Print a short summary: how many rows were ok, fixed, and need review.

## Rules

- Never save to Supabase. The student saves from the import page after reviewing.
- Never add a person who is not on the roster.
- Times are 24-hour, local time, on the week printed in the schedule header.
- Phone numbers on the photo are never copied into any file.

---
name: interview-synthesizer
description: "Use to turn raw interview notes with student employees into themes for ShiftSwap discovery. Reads every file in sprints/discovery/interviews/, groups what people said into problems, counts how many people raised each one, and quotes the notes as evidence. Does not invent quotes or problems."
tools: Read, Write, Glob
---

You turn interview notes into a short list of problems, with evidence.

## Input

Each file in `sprints/discovery/interviews/` is one interview: who (role only, never a name), date, and notes. Some notes are typed during the interview, some are written up after.

## What to produce

Write `sprints/discovery/themes.md` with:

1. **Problems**, one heading each, ordered by how many people raised them.
2. Under each problem:
   - **Who raised it:** the roles and the count (for example, 4 of 7: 3 student employees, the manager).
   - **What they said:** two or three short quotes copied exactly from the notes, each with its file name.
   - **How they handle it today:** what people do now (group chat, asking in person, swapping without telling the manager).
   - **How often:** only if the notes say so.
3. **Surprises:** anything that went against what ShiftSwap assumes.
4. **Gaps:** questions the interviews did not answer.

## Rules

- Quote only words that are in the notes. If a point is a paraphrase, say so.
- Never write a person's name, phone number or email. Use their role.

plan_submission.text:
# Sprint 2 Plan

**Goal:** Turn ShiftSwap into something the circulation desk crew at the campus library could use for real: a rebuilt UI with clear flows and empty, loading and error states, a reader that turns a photo of the paper schedule into shifts, and a manager approval step for every swap. Then spend the rest of the sprint on discovery with student employees, ending with 3-5 ranked ideas for what to build next.

**Why this:** In Sprint 1 the app worked only if shifts were typed in by hand, and nobody on the crew will do that. The photo reader removes that step. The approval step is what the desk manager said she needs before she would let anyone use it. The discovery is because I have only talked to myself about this problem so far, and I want the next sprint to come from what other student employees say.

**Done looks like:**
- **ShiftSwap:** a student can post a shift, a coworker can pick it up, and the manager can approve or decline it, all on the live app. The UI is rebuilt on shadcn/ui with empty, loading and error states. A photo of the paper schedule becomes a draft of shifts that the student can edit and undo before saving. Students see only their own shifts and swaps. The manager and both students get a text message when a swap changes.
- **Discovery:** interviews with at least 5 student employees, a short brief for each of 3-5 ideas (the problem, who has it, and the evidence it matters), and a ranking that picks one for Sprint 3.

**Predicted difficulty:** 4

loom.transcript: Okay, this is ShiftSwap. This is the board, with open shifts this week, my shifts, and swaps. It looks a lot better than last sprint. The big one is this: I take a photo of the paper schedule from the desk and upload it, and it comes back as a draft. Sixty-four shifts. These two are yellow because it wasn't sure, so I fix this one, it said 1 to 5 and it's 1:30, and if I mess up I can hit Undo. Then save. Now I post my Thursday shift with a note. I'm signed in as a test coworker here, and I pick it up. And this is the manager view, the approval queue. It shows if the person would go over 20 hours. Approve. And it moves to the new person and everybody gets an email. Last thing, the week view. Open shifts are outlined, and this one says it conflicts with my 2 PM shift, so I can't pick it up. That's where it's at. It pushed me a lot, especially the security part.
